title: He was born and educated in India. Now he runs one of the world's biggest beer companies. November 14, 2026.
excerpt: From the scientist who founded India's palaeobotany institute 135 years after his birth, to an Indian-educated engineer now running a global brewing giant, November 14's two stories are about foundations built once that keep carrying weight decades later.
bodyHtml:
Today's two stories are more than a century apart but share a thread: a foundation built in one place that ends up carrying someone - or something - much further.

He spent his life reading the story written in stone - fossilized plants that proved India's past stretched back hundreds of millions of years

Birbal Sahni, born November 14, 1891, became India's foremost palaeobotanist. In 1946, he founded the Institute of Palaeobotany in Lucknow - today the Birbal Sahni Institute of Palaeosciences, still running as an autonomous body under India's Department of Science and Technology, eight decades after he built it.

He was born and educated in India. Now he runs one of the world's biggest beer companies

Rahul Goyal, born and educated in India, earned a mechanical engineering degree from Mysore University before building a career in the US that led to his appointment as President and CEO of Molson Coors Beverage Company - one of the world's largest brewers, with brands including Coors, Miller, and Blue Moon.

Two stories, one pattern: an institution that outlived its founder, and an engineering degree that carried someone to the top of a global company.
